checkpoints.quote: The server response was: 5.7.139 Authentication unsuccessful, basic authentication is disabled.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis clearly identifies the SMTP 535 authentication error as the actual cause of failed delivery.

checkpoints.quote: They do **not** cause SMTP authentication to fail.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis explains the DataProtection/XML encryptor warnings are routine startup warnings unrelated to SMTP failures.

checkpoints.quote: The dispatcher is hammering the same failed send every 5 seconds, and new messages accumulate behind it.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis cites the 991204 warning and explains the fixed 5s retry with no backoff/dead-letter causing head-of-line blocking.

checkpoints.quote: Approximately 100 messages added every 5–6 minutes.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis presents the growing backlog from 1412 to 2089 and quantifies the growth rate.

checkpoints.quote: The log only covers 18:02 onwards (post-restart). The original failure at ~14:00 is not captured.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis correctly notes the log cannot confirm the 14:00 event since it starts post-restart.

checkpoints.quote: Priya's suggestion to "just restart it again" will not resolve the issue.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis explains the prior restart at 18:02 did not stop the ongoing 535 errors, so another restart won't help.

checkpoints.quote: Inference (high confidence): Something changed on or around 14:00 on the SMTP server or the email provider — most likely a policy update that disabled basic auth in favour of OAuth2 or another mechanism.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis labels this as an inference and correctly suggests a provider-side auth policy change as the fix direction.

checkpoints.quote: **Identify why basic auth was disabled on `smtp.example.com`.**
checkpoints.reason: The analysis covers confirming the auth change and adding backoff/dead-letter, but never suggests retrieving the pre-18:02 container log to confirm the 14:00 start.

checkpoints.quote: Brief and self-resolved. Not the cause of the outage.

The analysis explicitly rejects the reporter's DataProtection/XML encryptor explanation as unrelated to the SMTP failures.
